comparisonClass: founder and three G3 terminals generated by one fixed Trellis route and inspected from left, front, right, and opposite views

casts.spatialRead: Coherent open annulus, dorsal canopy, articulated support field, and a suspended interior organ remain visible from front and opposite views.
The annulus survives with paired horned crown masses, lateral canopy plates, and multiple suspended organs legible around the object.
The founder upper-body ancestry remains while the support field widens into long articulated stilts and distinct ventral appendages.

The strongest terminal gestalt remains a coherent segmented annulus with lateral sensory spars, sparse supports, and an eccentric spatially separate interior organ visible from right and opposite views.

verdict.claim: A procedural founder can be cumulatively mutated into distinct terminal armatures whose ancestry and branch-specific gestalt survive fixed image hallucination and fixed Trellis conversion as coherent spatial creatures.

boundedDrift: The image and Trellis stages regularize the sparse tripod commitment into variable three- or four-support locomotor fields; exact support count is not inherited reliably in this assay.
The lateral-sail terminal moves its suspended organ eccentrically behind the annulus rather than keeping it centered, while retaining it as distinct geometry.
Surface material remains highly consistent because the prompt and seed are fixed; this helps causal comparison but does not establish material heredity.
nextPressure: Expand founder silhouette and mass-distribution diversity while preserving this receipt-bearing lineage route, then test whether controlled crosses between terminal basins inherit selectable structures without collapsing into one dominant parent.
